assumptions.cost: 5 bp ≥ $500M weekly dollar volume, 15 bp ≥ $50M, 40 bp ≥ $5M, else 100 bp, one way
assumptions.universe: stocks ≥ $5 as traded and ≥ $5M a week, a year of closes

survivorship: Today's companies only: delisted, merged and bankrupt stocks are missing, which flatters long stock rules.

rows.name: S&P 500 (SPY), bought and held
rows.rules: SPY held throughout, dividends reinvested.

rows.name: Equal-weighted universe (today's survivors)
rows.rules: Every stock of the universe, equal weight, rebalanced monthly — the benchmark for the stock rules, with the same survivorship as them.

rows.name: 60/40 stocks and Treasuries
rows.rules: 60% SPY and 40% long Treasuries (TLT), rebalanced monthly.

rows.name: Trend: S&P 500 above its 10-month average
rows.rules: At each month-end, hold SPY if it closed above its 40-week (≈ 10-month) average, else cash.

rows.name: Dual momentum (US, international, bonds)
rows.rules: Monthly: if SPY beat cash over 12 months, hold the stronger of SPY and EFA; otherwise long Treasuries (TLT).

rows.name: Time-series momentum across asset classes
rows.rules: Monthly: US large and small caps, developed and emerging markets, Treasuries, gold and oil (SPY, IWM, EFA, EEM, TLT, GLD, USO as each becomes available), long if its 12-month return is positive, short if negative, each sized to 30% volatility ÷ the number of assets, gross exposure up to 3×.

rows.name: Stock momentum, 12-1 (top decile)
rows.rules: Monthly: the tenth of the universe with the highest return from 12 months to 1 month ago, equal weight.

rows.name: Stock momentum, long winners and short losers
rows.rules: Monthly: long the top tenth by 12-1 month return, short the bottom tenth, equal weight (dollar neutral).

rows.name: Near the 52-week high (top decile)
rows.rules: Monthly: the tenth of the universe closest to its 52-week high, equal weight.

rows.name: Sector rotation: strongest sectors
rows.rules: Monthly: the three SPDR sector ETFs with the highest six-month return, equal weight.

rows.name: Low volatility (lowest fifth)
rows.paper: Ang, Hodrick, Xing and Zhang (2006); Baker, Bradley and Wurgler (2011)
rows.rules: Monthly: the fifth of the universe with the lowest volatility of weekly returns over the past year, equal weight.

rows.name: Earnings yield (cheapest fifth, SEC figures)
rows.rules: Monthly: the fifth of the universe with the highest trailing-12-month net income ÷ market value (both from the site's SEC data: quarters used 13 weeks after they end, the last month-end market value), profitable names only. From 2010.

rows.name: Profitability: highest return on equity (SEC figures)
rows.rules: Monthly: the fifth of the universe with the highest trailing-12-month net income ÷ equity (SEC figures, 13 weeks after the quarter), positive equity only. From 2010.

rows.name: 13F breadth: most new holders (site 13F data)
rows.rules: Monthly: the tenth of the universe whose count of 13F holders grew most in the latest quarter (new holders less exits ÷ holders), used from the 45-day filing deadline. The site's 13F history is short: under two years.

rows.name: Short-term reversal (weekly, long losers, short winners)
rows.rules: Weekly, among the 500 most traded stocks: long the tenth that fell most last week, short the tenth that rose most — a rule that trades all of its capital every week, so its costs show.

rows.name: Buy the dip: S&P 500 below its lower Bollinger band
rows.rules: Hold SPY for four weeks after a weekly close below its 20-week average less two standard deviations, else cash.

rows.name: Sell in May: S&P 500 from November to April
rows.rules: SPY from the start of November to the end of April, cash from May to October.

rows.name: January effect: small caps over large caps
rows.rules: In January only, long small caps (IWM) and short large caps (SPY), equal dollars; flat the rest of the year.

rows.name: Volatility-targeted S&P 500 (15%)
rows.rules: Monthly: SPY sized to 15% ÷ its volatility over the last 13 weeks, up to 2× (borrowing at cash + 0.5%).

rows.name: Risk parity: stocks, Treasuries, gold
rows.rules: Monthly: SPY, TLT and GLD weighted by one over their six-month volatility (no leverage).

rows.name: Pairs trading (distance method)
rows.rules: Every six months, the 20 same-sector pairs among the 400 most traded stocks whose normalized prices tracked most closely over the past year; a pair opens when its gap exceeds two standard deviations (long the laggard, short the leader, 1/20 of capital a leg) and closes when the gap closes or at six months.

rows.name: Ensemble: every rule, risk-weighted
rows.rules: Each month, every non-benchmark rule with a year of returns, weighted by one over its volatility over the past year (no rule is chosen by its past return); costs are those of the rules.
